months several new pieces of play
ground equipment. The Milford
Elementary Parent-Teacher Asso-
citation took an active interest in
the plans for increased playground
facilities and made a creditable fl
nancial contribution to the project.


The children's return to school
this year was made more pleasant
and enjoyable as they found on the
playground a variety of equipment
that challenged their agility. Seem
ingly endless lines soon formed at
each piece of equipment as the chill
dren quickly initiated the slides,
swings, see-saws and jungle-gyms.


The first day ended with a few
cuts and bruises, a few dresses
torn, and the seats of many trOus-
ers worn thin. AS is always the
case with large numbers partici-
pating in an activity of this ma
ture, certain rules and regulations
are necessary to insure fun with
safety. To this end an elementary
assembly was held at which time
Mr.. WilkersOn presented Mr. Maui
mann, the elementary physical edu-
cation instructor, who explained
to the children the proper use and
case of the playground equipment.
He reminded them that the equip
ment was made with children's
safety uppermost in the manufac-
turers' minds, and, therefore, there
would be no excuse for anyone
getting hurt if the equipment were
respected and given proper use.


Mr.. Naumann's remarks were
well received and a visit now tC
the playground will reveal the
slides, the swings, and the see-saws
being used in a very orderly man
ner. The children are to be con-
graduated on their splendid CO.
operation.

Mrs. John D. Sheehan, IS, one.
of the first yeomanettes of the
Navy in World War I. died yes
terday at Mount Alto Hospital.
She lived at 3043 p street NV.


The former Margaret Curry,
she was born in Leavenworth.
KanS. She enlisted as yeo-
manette in 1918 when she was
so because her three sons were
in the armed services. She was
assigned to the Bureau of Aero
nautics.


In 1919 she was said to have
become the first civilian en-
ploye of the Navy Bureau of
Aeronautics. retiring in 1898.
After Pearl Harbor was bombed
by the Japanese. Mrs. Sheehan
persuaded some admirals, who
had been junior officers in her
yeomanette days, to let her serve
again as a civilian in the Aero
nautics Bureau through World
War II.


She was a charter member of
q. S. S. Jacob Jones Post No. 2
of the American Legion.


Survivors are three sons, Frank
j. Sheehan, 2915 Connecticut
avenue NV. former Federal la
Dor conciliator and now manager
OF public relations and labor re-
lations for Safeway Stores, Inc,
and John c. and M. K. Sheehan.
both of st. Louis, Mo.


Funeral services will be held
at 10 a m. Friday at st. Thomas
the Apostle Catholic Church.
Twenty-Seventh street and
Woodley road NV. Burial will
be in Mount Olivet Cemetery.
